newsitem.title: USA: Dollar mixed at U.S. noon, rallies versus mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mixed at U.S. noon, rallies versus mark.

text.p: The dollar stood mixed at U.S. midday, extending its overnight gains versus the mark, but edging lower versus the yen in quiet trade.

But shortly after noon, the greenback rallied to a fresh session high when comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp added to growing doubts that German interest rates can go higher in the near term.
In a speech in Hamburg, Krupp said the mark's recent weakness was worrying, but that a German rate hike now would severely damage the economy.
Investors have discounted the possibility of either a German variable-rate repo tender on Tuesday or an outright rate hike at the Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday, dealers said.
"The market is not buying into the Bundesbank's ability to sustain any interest rate rise with the European economies so weak," said Talbot Young, vice president at Signet Bank in Richmond, Va.
The dollar stood higher at 1.8225/35 marks at midday, up from 1.8200/10 at the open, then powered as high as 1.8275 following the release of the Krupp comments.
Dollar/yen was slightly lower at midday at 117.71/76 from 117.90/00 at the open but up from Friday's close at 117.39/44.
The greenback was helped early by a solid opening for the Dow Jones industrials and tended to move in tandem with stocks in the morning session.
A sharp drop of 247 points in the Dow on Friday left the dollar battered and traders waiting for direction on Monday.
"All the New York guys saw what happened on Friday and they are staring themselves blind at Wall Street and what happens to the Dow," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank in New York.
The dollar pulled back from key technical resistance at 1.8270-75 marks in U.S. trade, prompting day traders to unload dollars and book profits, dealers said.
The dollar enjoyed good support at 1.8270 marks on Friday before ultimately breaking down and dealers said the greenback was struggling to get above that level on Monday.
"People are selling dollars that were bought at 1.8050 and 1.81 (marks). Those guys didn't buy to hold them to 1.86, they're selling them now," said Boman.
Dollar/yen held most of its gains overnight, but failed to push through 118 as mark/yen slipped toward its session low.
Many dealers continue to see 110 to 120 as the medium-term range for dollar/yen and bulls get cold feet each time it nears the top of that range, dealers said.
"I still think we're in that big range, which means we'll see selling up towards 119," said Mark Gargano, head of currency derivatives at First Union National Bank.
Despite the dollar's tidy rebound overnight, dealers said they expected more selling pressure in the near future after Friday's bruising losses and the early Monday decline.
"People might still be a little bit too long and we could see more selling," said Boman.
"But there should be good support at 1.80 (marks). People are going to be buying with both hands down there," he added.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.5105/15 Swiss francs from 1.5091/96 at the open. Sterling rose to $1.6085/95 from $1.6060/70. The greenback edged higher to Canadian $1.3881/86 from C$1.3872/77.
((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
